rubric_fields.label: Originalidade
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Identifique a contribuição e diferencie-a de conhecimento já estabelecido. Exija evidência no artigo para a alegação de novidade, sem presumir que novidade implique qualidade.

rubric_fields.label: Solidez
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Confronte conclusões com métodos, dados ou demonstrações apresentados. Verifique hipóteses, limitações e se o desenho permite a inferência alegada; adapte a exigência ao tipo de artigo.

rubric_fields.label: Substância
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Verifique se experimentos, provas, síntese ou análise sustentam a contribuição declarada. Considere a profundidade e a cobertura da evidência, sem confundir extensão do texto com substância.

rubric_fields.label: Clareza
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Verifique definições, organização e correspondência entre texto, tabelas e figuras. Aponte ambiguidades localizáveis e distinga problemas de redação de problemas científicos.

rubric_fields.label: Comparação
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Confira se os trabalhos e alternativas relevantes são discutidos de forma justa. Compare métodos, condições e limitações equivalentes; não exija experimentos de um artigo estritamente teórico.

rubric_fields.label: Impacto
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Relacione a contribuição a uma necessidade da área e ao alcance sustentado pelos resultados. Distinga relevância demonstrada de aplicações futuras ainda especulativas.

rubric_fields.label: Reprodutibilidade
rubric_fields.rubric_text: Verifique disponibilidade ou descrição suficiente de materiais, dados, procedimentos e parâmetros. Restrições éticas ou legais podem justificar acesso controlado; não exija divulgação de dados pessoais.

document_map.abstract: Detecting entailment between words is a key task for several NLP applications. Pre- vious work has largely focused on en- tailment between words out of context. We propose, instead, to address lexical entailment in context, providing exem- plar sentences to ground the meaning of words considered in the entailment rela- tion. We show that contextualized word representations constructed from existing word embeddings, and word-context simi- larity features lead to significant improve- ments over context-agnostic models on two novel entailment test sets, and also improve the state-of-the-art on the related task of detecting semantic relations in con- text (Shwartz and Dagan, 2015).

sections.title: 1 Introduction
sections.first_sentence: Many NLP applications require detecting relations between word meanings beyond synonymy and paraphrasing.

sections.title: 2 Defining Lexical Entailment in Context
sections.first_sentence: We frame the task of lexical entailment in context as a binary classification task on examples consist- ing of a 4-tuple (wl, wr, Cl, Cr), where wι and wr are two words, and ci and cr are sentences which illustrate each word usage.

sections.title: 3 Representing Words and their Contexts for Entailment
sections.first_sentence: How can we construct vector representations of the meaning of target words wι and wr in their respective exemplar contexts Cι and Cr?

sections.title: 3.1 Contextualized Word Representations
sections.first_sentence: Following Thater et al.

sections.title: 3.2 A Shared Vector Space for Words and Contexts: Context2vec
sections.first_sentence: An alternative approach to contextualizing word representations is to directly compare the repre- sentations of words with representations of con- texts.

sections.title: 4 Comparing Words and Contexts for Entailment
sections.first_sentence: Given words and context representations de- scribed above, how can we predict entailment?

sections.title: 4.1 Supervised Logistic Regression model
sections.first_sentence: Prior work on lexical entailment out of context suggests that the entailment relationship between words is a learnable function of the concatenation of their individual representations (Baroni et al., 2012; Turney and Mohammad, 2013).

sections.title: 4.2 Similarity Features
sections.first_sentence: We hypothesize that entailment relations hold be- tween related words and introduce similarity fea- tures to capture this non-directional relation be- tween words and contexts.

sections.title: 5 Evaluation Framework
sections.first_sentence: We evaluate our models of lexical entailment in context on three complementary datasets.

sections.title: 5.1 CONTEXT-PPDB
sections.first_sentence: The first dataset, CONTEXT-PPDB, is a fine-grained lexical inference dataset created using 375 word pairs from a subset of the English Paraphrase Database (Ganitkevitch et al., 2013; Pavlick et al., 2015b).

sections.title: 5.2 CONTEXT-WN
sections.first_sentence: In addition to CONTEXT-PPDB, we would like a test set for controlled analysis of lexical entailment in context.

sections.title: 5.3 Crosslingual dataset
sections.first_sentence: Our final dataset takes a cross-lingual view of lexical entailment in context.

sections.title: 6.1 Monolingual
sections.first_sentence: All experiments on CONTEXT-PPDB and CONTEXT-WN are with the default train/dev/test splits.

sections.title: 6.2 Crosslingual
sections.first_sentence: We evaluate our models on cross-lingual test set in a transfer setting by training on the training set of CONTEXT-PPDB.

sections.title: 7.1 CONTEXT-PPDB
sections.first_sentence: Representation-based features only A context-agnostic baseline (Baroni et al., 2012) based on the concatenation of the word type features for (ωι, wr) reaches F1 scores of 53.5 using Glove and 54 with Context2Vec (Table 4).

sections.title: 7.2 CONTEXT-WN
sections.first_sentence: We repeat all experiments on CONTEXT-WN (Table 4), except for those that require PPDB-specific features.

sections.title: 7.3 Cross-lingual dataset
sections.first_sentence: Results on the cross-lingual dataset are similar to monolingual results (Table 5).

sections.title: 8 Analysis
sections.first_sentence: The experiments in Section 7 attest to the overall strength of our features.

sections.title: 8.1 Sensitivity to context
sections.first_sentence: How sensitive are our models to changes in contexts?

sections.title: 8.2 Sensitivity to Entailment Direction
sections.first_sentence: To quantitatively evaluate our claim of our features learning to discriminate directionality, we report results on the subset of CONTEXT-WN that consists of all positive examples, and the equivalent number of flipped negative examples generated in Step 4.

sections.title: 8.3 Contextualized Masks
sections.first_sentence: We also hypothesized that masked contextual-ized representations based on the full volume of the context using min and max operations (Sec-tion 3.1) better capture salient context dimensions than the more usual vector averaging approach.

sections.first_sentence: We proposed to address lexical entailment in con-text, providing exemplar sentences to ground the meaning of words being considered for entail-ment.
